2\. Windows pinning can fail verification 🐞 Bug ☼ Reliability 
cmd_pin writes the complete workflow using Path.write_text, which translates line endings on
Windows rather than preserving the committed bytes of lines it did not change. In a clone without
Git line-ending normalization, the resulting commit changes every line to CRLF and
check_release_commit rejects it because its content is not the parent workflow with only two pins
substituted.
Agent Prompt ``` ## Issue description The maintainer’s `pin` command can translate the whole workflow to CRLF on Windows, causing its release commit to fail the two-line-only verification. ## Fix Focus Areas - scripts/release.py[83-87] - hb/release.py[303-306] ## Recommended Fix Write the pinned workflow as UTF-8 bytes, or open it with newline translation disabled, so every unchanged byte remains identical to the committed workflow. Add a test covering the byte-preservation requirement. ``` ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools
